notes: Corrected: the supplied *of* in *thou mayest eat of grapes* moves from `עֲנָבִים` to the verb `אָכַלְתָּ`. Rule 33 governs a function word supplied for an adverbial accusative or an appositional or measure nominal; `עֲנָבִים` is the bare direct object of the eating, so rule 44's preposition supplied to reach the verb's own object governs, as in `תְּבַצְּעִי רֵעַיִךְ` → *hast greedily gained of thy neighbors*.
The object of *put* is unexpressed in Hebrew, so the supplied *any* is `added` (rule 44).
`כֶרֶם רֵעֶךָ` is written as an English possessive, so the construct keeps only *vineyard* and the suffix's *thy* stands before the possessor's word (rules 18, 29).
